title: Dict additions
prompt_markdown: Which is the correct way to add a key to a dict `d`?

content.explanation: Assignment via index syntax adds or updates a key.

title: Set features
prompt_markdown: Which of the following is true about sets?

content.explanation: Sets only store hashable (immutable) elements to ensure uniqueness.

title: List vs Tuple
prompt_markdown: What is a key difference between lists and tuples?

content.explanation: Tuples cannot be changed once created.

title: Dict fetching
prompt_markdown: Which method avoids a KeyError if a key is missing?

content.explanation: get() returns None instead of raising an error.

title: Tuples as keys
prompt_markdown: Explain why tuples are preferred over lists as dictionary keys.

content.reference_answer: Dictionary keys must be hashable. Tuples are immutable and therefore hashable, whereas lists are mutable and cannot be used as keys.

title: Set vs List
prompt_markdown: When should you use a set instead of a list?

content.reference_answer: Use a set when you need to ensure elements are unique, or when you need fast O(1) membership testing.
